Use for coordination, delegation, advice, QA, recovery, and completion decisions. --- # Northstar Deliver useful, verified work with low total effort and rework. Preserve authority, dirty work and the full requested outcome; follow the [delivery contract](#delivery-contract). **Start with the next useful action.** Read the applicable instructions and current task state, identify the next unmet criterion, and make the smallest change or distinguishing check that advances it. Before expanding research, planning or team setup, produce a relevant artifact, inspect a real result, or demonstrate the specific blocker. More process records are not delivery. Detailed guidance below is for its stated trigger; do not read every linked reference before acting. ## Preserve task continuity and accumulate evidence More context should refine project understanding without replacing the requested outcome. Apply this check at task entry, after context compaction/resumption, and before changing direction or claiming completion. - **Keep one durable anchor.** For sustained work, maintain a compact current-state block in the existing project task/goal record: full Ask, acceptance and remaining obligations; user decisions/constraints with their source; verified artifacts/checks; unresolved assumptions; failed attempts/recovery allowance; and one next action tied to an unmet criterion. Keep its path in the handoff or existing project index so a new context can find it. Small one-turn work needs only its request and handoff; promote it to the existing durable record if it grows across turns or needs recovery. - **Learn from evidence.** Distinguish user requirements/decisions, observed facts (source plus revision/environment where relevant), hypotheses, and unknowns. Integrate new evidence into the current understanding; mark contradicted conclusions superseded with the reason instead of leaving conflicting facts active. Preserve material decisions, rejected approaches and unresolved requirements when shortening history. Trace mandatory acceptance to the user request or applicable project rules. Label agent-added design choices as proposals or working assumptions; do not promote them into user requirements or retained user decisions. Summaries and worker claims are pointers, not verification; do not fill missing details with plausible inventions or treat repeated claims as new evidence. - **Save at meaningful boundaries.** Update the same anchor after a user correction, material finding, accepted step, failed approach, direction change, and before a handoff or anticipated compaction. Read back saved changes before claiming persistence. Do not depend on a compaction warning arriving; maintain state during work. Keep detailed logs elsewhere and link them only when needed; do not grow an append-only transcript or update a record on every tool call. - **Rehydrate before acting.** After resumption, read the anchor and relevant user steering, then inspect the actual artifact/diff and any evidence whose freshness affects the next action. Reconcile mismatches before dependent edits. If the record is missing or stale, reconstruct from accessible user instructions and artifacts, label gaps unknown, and ask only when missing information changes scope, authority or correctness. Never silently choose among multiple plausible active tasks. - **Rethink the method, preserve the outcome.** After surprising evidence, a user correction, repeated failure, or a completed increment, compare the original ask with the whole current result, not just the subtask in view. State what changed in project understanding and whether the current method still serves the outcome; test a disconfirming fact or simpler alternative when it could change the decision. Revise a disproven plan within existing authority without silently narrowing acceptance. If nothing material changed, continue without ceremonial replanning. - **Brake on drift signals.** If an action cannot be tied to a remaining user criterion, a proposed change contradicts a confirmed decision, an accepted workflow regresses, or a disproven approach repeats without new evidence, stop dependent edits before making the next patch. Preserve the diff; compare the original ask, last verified state and new evidence; name the mismatch and take one bounded corrective step under the existing recovery allowance. Resume that route only when the contradiction is resolved or explicitly retained as an unknown with a safe next check. Continue independent authorized work; this is not a new user-approval gate. Do not reset recovery counts by changing agents or context. - **Protect the acceptance baseline.** Keep required user-visible behavior and meaningful checks stable while diagnosing failure. Do not delete a failing check, weaken its assertion, relabel required work optional, or replace real evidence with a mock just to obtain a pass. Change an incorrect check only when the original requirement or new evidence justifies it; record that reason and retain coverage of the required outcome. After each complete increment, check the changed behavior and affected previously working workflow before stacking more changes. - **Check direction.** Before a new work phase, delegation, broad investigation or final answer, identify which remaining criterion the action advances and which evidence supports it. An unrelated action is deferred; repeated investigation uses the existing recovery allowance. A status question or side question does not replace the task: answer it and resume. Apply explicit user changes or cancellations, preserve unaffected obligations, and record what was superseded. Do not let the latest tool output redefine the goal. This is a persistent working practice, not an enforced runtime guard or a guarantee against hallucination. It works only when the host loads these instructions and the agent reads/writes the record. If storage is unavailable, follow the existing [storage boundary](references/goal-driven-engineering.md#keep-goal-state-project-owned), disclose unsaved state, and carry a concise handoff; never claim durable learning from chat alone. ## Delivery contract This is the shared default for all six skills, their references and templates. Companion instructions specialize it; they must not create a second workflow or approval chain. Explicit task requirements and platform boundaries still govern. - **Focus the existing core.** Choose one current commitment: the existing user workflow whose completion or repair delivers the most useful value. Treat 80/20 as a prioritization heuristic, not a measured ratio or permission to drop requirements. Add a feature, role, tool or abstraction only when it is needed for this commitment; park other ideas. - **Finish before expanding.** Keep Ask / Acceptance / Remaining in the existing task record. Build the smallest complete result and run relevant checks. Use one nonauthor review when required or when it can change acceptance: material user/data/security risk, cross-component integration, unresolved uncertainty or visual judgment. Otherwise the commander accepts small, reversible work when its scope is attributable and relevant checks pass. If scope or evidence cannot be established, keep acceptance unverified or obtain the required review. This is accountable acceptance, not an independent verdict. Repair failed criteria; keep accepted scope closed unless new evidence warrants reopening it. Reuse evidence only while its artifact, environment and claim remain applicable. - **Continue while the next step earns its cost.** Continue when an authorized step can satisfy a required criterion, remove a material risk or resolve uncertainty that changes the next action. Stop optional polish, research, consultation and process changes when their expected benefit no longer justifies time, tokens, coordination and rework. State the concrete reason; no invented scores or fixed improvement quotas. Diminishing returns never turns an unmet requirement into a pass: retain it and use bounded recovery or report its exact dependency. - **One approval owner.** Name one commander agent as the sole approval/decision owner. Covered actions are already authorized by the user's standing grant; the commander directs them without fresh approval, and workers execute within scope without asking the user or opening another approval queue. The commander resolves exceptions within its delegated authority. QA supplies an independent verdict, not another permission gate. Ask the user only for a decision explicitly reserved to them or authority the grant does not cover. An agent cannot approve beyond the user's grant or override a platform denial; report the exact boundary and continue independent authorized work. - **Subtract process.** Default to one owner. Add workers or reviewers only when required or when their value exceeds coordination and integration cost. Load a companion only for the current need. Reuse one result, decision and evidence record. Consult council for a material unresolved decision, not reassurance. Stop adding goals and mechanisms while the current commitment can be finished. ## Discover and deliver the useful outcome When the customer, problem, value or product direction is uncertain, use [product discovery](references/product-discovery.md) to choose the smallest informative test before committing to a build. A mockup, technical proof of concept or MVP may each be useful, but none is a mandatory stage. Apply the delivery steps below to the chosen outcome, including discovery when that is the task. For a consequential business plan, market/research decision, go-to-market or pricing choice, operating model, or scenario analysis needing adversarial examination and economics, use [business planning and adversarial research](references/business-planning.md). Product discovery tests a specific product assumption; business planning integrates buyers, evidence, alternatives, operations and financial scenarios. Neither is a stage gate for a clearly specified delivery. 1. **Resume the actual request.** Recover original requirements, authorized changes, existing evidence, relevant lessons and failed attempts. Use the project's current records; do not restart accepted work or create missing Northstar folders just to begin. 2. **Define the finish.** Name the intended user workflow, environment and observable acceptance. Distinguish the full requested endpoint from this increment and retain remaining obligations. A request and short handoff suffice for small work. For uncertain products, identify the riskiest assumption and test it with a bounded usable increment. 3. **Build the next complete step.** Reuse existing tools and supported capabilities. Research a concrete decision that blocks implementation; otherwise implement. Choose reversible details within the mandate. If delegation is worthwhile, give the worker the target artifact, acceptance check, first action, authority, write scope and deadline, then dispatch promptly. For a small CLI assignment, use a host-enforced five-minute artifact checkpoint and ten-minute handoff deadline with one targeted check. Longer work names intermediate artifacts and a real deadline. Stop a missed or blocked worker, preserve partial work and resolve the cause; do not let it run serial diagnostics or retry unchanged. 4. **Verify and repair.** Check changed behavior and plausible failures. Load [Codex QA](../codex-qa/SKILL.md) when the review threshold applies, including visual inspection when relevant. Otherwise the commander accepts attributable, small and reversible work from relevant checks and the scoped diff. Repair failed criteria and recheck affected scope when required; reuse evidence. A build, HTTP 200, mock or worker claim alone is insufficient. 5. **Deliver the requested endpoint.** Reconcile every original requirement against evidence and the reviewer verdict when required, otherwise the commander's acceptance. Mark each passed, unmet or unverified. Keep required work open; a narrower review cannot discharge it. Deliver with checks and material limits, and do not invent another increment after completion. When sustained or repeated testing is needed to assess an agent harness or model's reliability, use the standalone `soak-testing` skill if available and the test is within the user's authorized scope and budget. Soak is optional, not a routine delivery gate; distinguish synthetic, short-run and real-target evidence. If the skill or framework is unavailable, use an appropriate authorized alternative where possible and report any unmet duration or target evidence. The separate [Soak framework](https://github.com/stancsz/soak) provides its own skill; its installation and readiness are not implied by Northstar. Use [Task Completion Review](../task-completion-review/SKILL.md) only when a substantive finish, wait or escalation decision remains uncertain after applying this contract; otherwise decide directly and reuse current evidence. Preserve security, privacy, data integrity and necessary failure handling. A local MVP does not establish release readiness, business viability or demand. For explicitly local work, do not invent deployment obligations. ## Six skills, one coordinated package Install sibling directories `northstar`, `codex-qa`, `codex-subagents`, `codex-advisor`, `claude-code-subagents` and `task-completion-review` together. Load only the companion needed for the next decision: | Trigger | Load | | --- | --- | | Independent acceptance is required or materially useful | [Codex QA](../codex-qa/SKILL.md) | | Worthwhile parallel work, CLI delegation or independent reviewer setup | [Codex Subagents](../codex-subagents/SKILL.md) | | Documented capability risk, art/image/aesthetic work or a concrete expert blocker | [Codex Advisor](../codex-advisor/SKILL.md); apply its material-decision triggers | | Requested Claude Code or useful independent Claude capacity | [Claude Code Subagents](../claude-code-subagents/SKILL.md) | | Decide whether substantive work may finish, continue, wait or escalate | [Task Completion Review](../task-completion-review/SKILL.md) | Bundling does not require every lane or parallel implementation. When independent acceptance applies, keep it separate from authorship. The optional [Windows app recovery](../windows-app-recovery/SKILL.md) utility installs separately. Advisor service, optional Pi and CLI/provider prerequisites are separate from skill installation. ## Use with other agents Use these practices in Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode or another agent. `Codex` names identify origin, not a restriction. Preserve the six sibling names; adapt invocation, configuration and tools to the host's actual capabilities, reading the entrypoint directly if necessary. Preserve intent, authority, recovery history and independent acceptance where required. If a capability is unavailable, continue applicable work and identify that gap; do not invent a reviewer or claim runtime compatibility from installation. The Claude adapter specifically describes Codex-to-Claude CLI delegation. ## Prefer local LiteLLM inference for agent work Route Codex and Claude CLI workers' primary inference through `http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1` by default. Use the gateway's dynamic `default` alias unless the task selects any other model ID or alias supported by that Subroute endpoint; never pin a backend model in shared guidance. The parent verifies a new/reconfigured client and required tool path with bounded smoke evidence before dispatch, keeps credentials private, and passes the proven endpoint and model selection to the worker. A listening port, model list or parent completion does not prove child routing. Follow the [CLI setup and capture instructions](../codex-subagents/SKILL.md#allocate-capability-and-cost) when dispatching; do not change global settings or force an incompatible protocol. Preserve the current diff and last verified behavior. Test one causal change at a time; remove only your disproven experiments, never others' work. 3.
